exam_scheme.note: The National Common Entrance Test (NCET) is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) on behalf of the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) for admission into the 4-Year Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP) — leading to dual-major Bachelor of Arts B.Ed. (B.A. B.Ed.), Bachelor of Science B.Ed. (B.Sc. B.Ed.), and Bachelor of Commerce B.Ed. (B.Com. B.Ed.) degrees — across premier multidisciplinary higher education institutions including Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), National Institutes of Technology (NITs), Regional Institutes of Education (RIEs), Central Universities, and Government Colleges. The examination is conducted as a Computer Based Test (CBT) consisting of 160 multiple-choice questions (to be attempted from 181 total questions) carrying a total of 640 marks, with a test duration of 120 minutes. The examination comprises four distinct sections: Section 1 (Languages: candidates choose 2 languages from 38 languages, 20 questions each = 40 questions), Section 2 (Domain Specific Subjects: candidates choose 3 domain subjects from 26 offered disciplines, 25 questions each = 75 questions), Section 3 (General Test: mandatory, 25 questions), and Section 4 (Teaching Aptitude: mandatory, 20 questions). Marking scheme: 4 marks awarded for each correct response, negative marking of 1 mark deducted for each incorrect response (-1), and 0 marks for unattempted questions.
